description: Pre-LLM statutory rules. Each rule has a deterministic trigger (matched against the raw profile) and a deterministic action (mutates sanitized_profile or appends to triggered_rules). The engine never calls an LLM.

rules.rationale: California Proposition 103 prohibits use of credit information in personal lines homeowners underwriting/rating.

Under Prop 103 the three mandatory rating factors are driving record (auto), miles driven (auto), and years of driving experience. For homeowners, age may be used only as a non-primary factor and never as a sole basis for rating or underwriting.
Insurers writing residential property in California must offer earthquake coverage (typically through the California Earthquake Authority) at every new business and renewal.

rules.citation: Cal. Ins. Code §2051.5 (additional living expense minimums)
rules.rationale: California requires Loss-of-Use / Additional Living Expense coverage of at least 24 months following a declared disaster (12 months for non-disaster losses); the 24-month floor binds for catastrophe perils.
California prescribes a standard fire policy form (§2071) that establishes baseline insuring agreements and conditions for fire coverage in residential policies.

rules.citation: Cal. Ins. Code §10090 et seq. (FAIR Plan Act)
rules.rationale: When the property sits in a CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zone of High or Very High, the admitted market often declines and the FAIR Plan (basic peril) plus a Difference-In-Conditions wrap is the operative route.

Florida statute requires that when credit information is unavailable for an applicant, the insurer must apply a neutral credit factor (treated as 1.0×) rather than penalising the applicant. This is the load-bearing protection for Profile B.
Personal residential policies in Florida must offer the insured a choice of hurricane deductibles: a flat $500 (where dwelling ≤ $250K) and percentages of 2%, 5%, and 10% of Coverage A.

rules.citation: Fla. Stat. §627.706 (Citrus / catastrophic ground cover collapse)
rules.rationale: Florida law requires every personal lines residential policy to include catastrophic ground cover collapse (CGCC) coverage; broader sinkhole coverage is offered as an option with a 14-point rejection notice.
Sinkhole loss coverage beyond CGCC is optional in Florida; insurers must offer it with a 14-point statutory rejection notice if the insured declines.

Florida requires insurers to apply mitigation discounts for wind-resistive construction features documented on form OIR-B1-1802 (roof shape/cover/deck, opening protection, secondary water resistance). Discount can reach ~45% of wind premium.

rules.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B7-3-02 (property insurance requirements)
rules.rationale: GSE-eligible mortgages require the dwelling coverage limit be at least the lesser of replacement cost value or the unpaid principal balance, with replacement-cost (not actual-cash-value) settlement.

rules.citation: Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973 (42 U.S.C. §4012a)
rules.rationale: Federally-backed mortgages on properties in a Special Flood Hazard Area must carry flood insurance (NFIP or private equivalent meeting Biggert-Waters acceptability).

rules.citation: Product scope: California and Florida only
rules.rationale: This system's statutory engine and rate filings cover California and Florida only; profiles in other states are routed to an informational-only response and confidence is capped.
